issues.reason: Thematic roles gives Patient only to an object the action creates, destroys, consumes or physically changes, and threads left on a lantern are deposited unaltered, so the yes/no change test — and its stated 'when the test is unclear, default to Theme' — selects (Theme sk_leave_1 sk_thread_1).
The s7_leave_rule conclusion carries the identical (Patient (sk_leave $x) sk_thread_1) conjunct, so the same unlicensed change-of-state claim is asserted once per nightmoth.

Comparatives & degree defines Ordinal's third slot as the ordering scale — the associated event ((Ordinal priya 1 respond)) or an explicit -est dimension ((Ordinal x 3 tall)) — so filling it with the entity's own class word invents a scale no word supplies and, under the stated 'superlative is the rank-1 special case' reading, yields the ill-typed (Most cauldron ...).

gaps_confirmed: Capitalized bare-plural kind word used as an ordinary role label ('Keepers lit the lanterns'): the capitalized-common-noun default is declared singular-collective only and the plural carve-out covers only a label referring as a name, so no test decides between a Name-only individual and an ordinary bare-plural group witness.

An ordinal used as a bare identifying label inside a fixed set ('the second cauldron'): no event and no -est dimension is stated to fill Ordinal's scale slot, and the reserved 'unspecified' filler is licensed only in Measure-family slots, so the construction has no licensed form at all.

Bare MASS-noun arguments in episodic clauses ('burned mire-essence', 'produced mist-light', 'Mire-essence formed in the second cauldron'): the bare-PLURAL rule states when a participating set takes a group witness versus a bare kind filler, but there is no mass analog, so the same noun can land on either.

No object-side under-distribution form: the per-member rule replicates the whole object (a definite plural group or a shared singular witness), so 'Keepers lit the lanterns of the East Row' derives that each keeper lit every lantern, and the instruction set offers no 'between them' shape to weaken it.
new_gaps: Day-of-year dating in a month-less calendar ('on day 3 of Year 1'): the Time term (Day <n>) is defined as day-of-month (June 5, 2021 -> (Day 5)), so a day counted within a year has no distinct carrier and the Day+Year pair emitted here is indistinguishable from a day-of-month reading — which also leaves the seeded date-ordering rules (year, same-year month, same-year-month day) unable to order day 3 before day 4.

Verb/noun homograph collapse: lemmatization maps every surface form of a word to one symbol with no sense slot, so 'lit' and the head noun of 'mist-light' both land on `light` — this parse holds (Member sk_light_1 light) for the lighting event beside (Inheritance mist_light light) for the substance, and any rule or query over `light` conflates the two.
defect_summary: The compliant form for s7_leave_pat is (Theme sk_leave_1 sk_thread_1); the compliant form for s7_leave_rule is the same rule with (Theme (sk_leave $x) sk_thread_1) in the conclusion; for 'the second cauldron' NO compliant form is licensed — Ordinal's scale slot admits only an associated event or an explicit -est dimension and `unspecified` is barred outside Measure-family slots, so the only rule-conforming output is (Member sk_cauldron_1 cauldron) with the ordinal label dropped and recorded as the gap above.
notes: The s1 and s13 per-member rules instantiate the reviewer's fourth gap as an actual over-assertion — each keeper is derived to have lit the entire lantern group — and s3's rule does the same with the single mist-light witness. The mire_essence bare-kind / witness split the reviewer notes in passing is defensible rather than defective: s3 and s11 mint witnesses precisely because later definite mentions corefer with them, while s2's object is the non-specific kind filler the 'grows wheat' clause licenses.
